newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU crude stocks seen rising, products a puzzle.
newsitem.headline: EU crude stocks seen rising, products a puzzle.

text.p: European oil stock inventories figures for the end of May, to be released on Tuesday, are widely expected to show a crude build, but fine product stock movements are hard to estimate, analysts said this week.
Most believed the crude build will be sizeable, but is likely to be somewhat short of the 13 million barrel rise seen in April.

"Crude must surely have risen. We've seen a strong build in the U.S. over the past month and it should follow that pattern. We've also had some refinery maintenance in Europe," said Peter Bogin of Paris-based Cambridge Energy Research Associates.
Analysts cited plentiful reasons for the rise in crude stocks.

Output from OPEC countries, which rose in April, remained high. West African crude, originally earmarked for the Asia Pacific region, has ended up in Europe and maintenance in the North Sea was expected to have had little impact.
The strong market contango also reflected growing supply.
By contrast, product stock levels appeared difficult to predict.
"Gas oil is a huge question mark," said Leslie Owens of oil consultants Petroleum Economics.

However, while the direction may be uncertain, the signs were certainly not bullish. The heavy buying in April into the Asia Pacific region, largely by Hin Leong Trading, petered out by May. Continental European demand appeared to have been low.
Whichever direction middle distillate stocks move, one thing seems certain: the level will remain historically very high.
"(Distillate stocks) were some 10 million barrels above the three year maximum.... We're back into oversupply again," said Geoff Pyne, oil analyst at bank UBS.

This may leave gasoline as the only product whose stocks fell, as exports drew material from the region. However, here too, the picture is far from bullish. Low overall demand means analysts expect only a slight draw.
The figures for the 15 countries of the European Union plus Norway will be published by Euroilstock at 1300 GMT on Tuesday.
